Kādambakakalpa
alchemy. Īśvara-Pārvatī-saṁvāda; eulogizing a certain Kādamba hill on the Śatruñjaya mountains in Saurāṣṭra, whose mud is to be used in alchemy.

Kādambara(svīkaraṇa)sūtra
Kāmaśāstra in 31 sūtras on the aphrodisiac use of drinking. ascribed to King Purūravas. RASB. XIV. 4.

Kādambarī
prose romance in two parts, pūrvabhāga an. uttarabhāga, the former by Bāṇa Bhaṭṭa of the court of King Harṣavardhana of Kanauj, A. D. 606-648, an. the latter completed, after his death by his son Bhūṣaṇa Bhaṭṭa or Pulina(nda) Bhaṭṭa according to some mss. an. Dhanapāla's Tilakamañjarī.
Its plot taken from Guṇāḍhya's Bṛhatkathā (Somadeva's Kathāsaritsāgara 59. 22-178; Kṣemendra's Bṛhatkathāmañjarī 16. 183 ff.); the son not only closely followed his father's style but knew also the father's plan of the story. See WZKM. 15. p. 213 ff. For a. [Page334-a. bibliography, indexes an. concordances, regarding Bāṇa an. Kādambarī see A. A. M. Scharpe, Bāṇa's Kādambarī, Louvain, 1937, p.. 1-108.
